--- title: "Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide Meta-Analysis" subtitle: "Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of PTCy vs alternative GVHD prophylaxis platforms" date: 2026-05-29 --- ## Abstract ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Background.** Post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) has become widely adopted for GVHD prophylaxis in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation, yet comprehensive quantitative evidence synthesis across survival, GVHD, and infection outcomes — and across comparator regimens — has been lacking. **Methods.** We conducted a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of 251 studies (14 RCTs) comparing PTCy to (1) CNI+MTX/MMF-based regimens (Comparison 1) and (2) ATG-based regimens (Comparison 2). Primary outcomes included overall survival (OS), non-relapse mortality (NRM), acute GVHD grade II–IV, CMV reactivation, bloodstream infection (BSI), and invasive fungal infection (IFI). Steroid-mediation models (M2) tested whether GVHD-driven steroid exposure confounded observed effects. **Results.** PTCy was associated with improved OS (C1: OR 0.79 [0.73–0.85]; C2: OR 0.84 [0.76–0.93]) and reduced aGVHD (C1: OR 0.67; C2: OR 0.58) across both comparators. NRM benefit was substantially or completely mediated by steroid exposure in both comparisons. CMV reactivation showed a direction reversal: increased with PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.26 [1.07–1.47]) but decreased vs ATG (OR 0.96 [0.80–1.16]), consistent with a T-cell depletion depth hierarchy. BSI risk was elevated in both comparisons (C1: OR 1.87; C2: MH OR 2.03). **Conclusions.** PTCy provides consistent survival and GVHD advantages regardless of comparator. The CMV direction reversal establishes that infection risk is determined by the relative depth of T-cell depletion, not by any intrinsic PTCy property. NRM benefit is steroid-mediated. GRADE certainty is LOW for OS and aGVHD, VERY LOW for other outcomes. ::: --- ## Executive Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pd <- do.call(rbind, list( or_os, or_m2_os, or_nrm, or_m2_nrm, or_agvhd, or_cmv, or_m2_cmv, or_bsi, or_ifi, or_c2_os, or_c2_m2_os, or_c2_nrm, or_c2_agvhd, or_c2_cmv, or_c2_m2_cmv )) |> as_tibble() |> mutate( outcome = factor(outcome, levels = rev(c("OS", "NRM", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "CMV", "BSI", "IFI"))), comparison = factor(comparison, levels = c("C1: PTCy vs CNI+MTX", "C2: PTCy vs ATG")), label = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", or, lo, hi), y_num = as.numeric(outcome), y_pos = y_num + ifelse(model == "M2", -0.15, 0.15) ) ggplot(pd, aes(x = or, y = y_pos, shape = model, fill = model)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = jama_grey, linewidth = 0.4) + geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = model), size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) + geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = label), hjust = -0.05, size = 2.5, colour = jama_black, show.legend = FALSE, nudge_y = 0.25) + scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.5, 2, 3)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:6, labels = rev(c("OS", "NRM", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "CMV", "BSI", "IFI"))) + scale_shape_manual(values = c("M1" = 16, "M2" = 21), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = "white"), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + facet_wrap(~ comparison) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.25, 5.5)) + labs(x = "Odds Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL, shape = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Bayesian random-effects models (binomial family, brms). BSI C2 estimate is Mantel-Haenszel (not shown).") + theme_jama(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Bayesian meta-analysis — PTCy effect across outcomes and comparators. Filled circles represent direct-effect models (M1); open circles represent steroid-adjusted models (M2). The dashed vertical line marks OR = 1 (no effect). OR < 1 favours PTCy for all outcomes.](index_files/figure-html/fig-exec-summary-1.svg){#fig-exec-summary} ::: ::: ### Key Findings ::: {.key-finding} **1. Survival and GVHD benefit.** PTCy was associated with reduced overall mortality and acute GVHD in both Comparison 1 (vs CNI+MTX/MMF) and Comparison 2 (vs ATG). The effect was consistent in magnitude and direction across comparators. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **2. NRM is steroid-mediated.** The apparent NRM benefit was substantially or completely attenuated after adjusting for GVHD-driven steroid exposure in both comparisons, indicating that PTCy reduces NRM indirectly — through fewer GVHD episodes and less corticosteroid toxicity. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **3. CMV direction reversal.** PTCy increased CMV reactivation vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.26) but *decreased* it vs ATG (OR 0.96). This reversal confirms that CMV risk is ordered by the depth of T-cell depletion (CNI < PTCy < ATG), not by any intrinsic PTCy property. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **4. BSI elevated in both comparisons.** Bloodstream infection risk was approximately doubled with PTCy regardless of comparator (C1: OR 1.87; C2: MH OR 2.03), though the C2 estimate is based on only 3 studies with heterogeneous definitions. ::: ### Summary of Evidence ::: {#tbl-exec-summary .cell tbl-cap='Summary of primary outcomes across both comparisons.'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Build dynamically from posterior draws get_k <- function(slug, mdl = "m1") { if (!is.null(t2)) { row <- t2 |> filter(slug == !!slug, model == !!mdl) if (nrow(row) > 0) return(list(k = row$k, n = row$n_total)) } list(k = NA, n = NA) } summary_tbl <- tibble::tribble( ~Outcome, ~Comparison, "OS", "C1", "OS", "C2", "NRM", "C1", "NRM", "C2", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C1", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C2", "CMV", "C1", "CMV", "C2", "BSI", "C1", "IFI", "C1" ) |> mutate( `OR [95% CrI]` = c( fmt_or(or_os$or, or_os$lo, or_os$hi), fmt_or(or_c2_os$or, or_c2_os$lo, or_c2_os$hi), fmt_or(or_nrm$or, or_nrm$lo, or_nrm$hi), fmt_or(or_c2_nrm$or, or_c2_nrm$lo, or_c2_nrm$hi), fmt_or(or_agvhd$or, or_agvhd$lo, or_agvhd$hi), fmt_or(or_c2_agvhd$or, or_c2_agvhd$lo, or_c2_agvhd$hi), fmt_or(or_cmv$or, or_cmv$lo, or_cmv$hi), fmt_or(or_c2_cmv$or, or_c2_cmv$lo, or_c2_cmv$hi), fmt_or(or_bsi$or, or_bsi$lo, or_bsi$hi), fmt_or(or_ifi$or, or_ifi$lo, or_ifi$hi) ), `P(directional)` = c( sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_os$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_os$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_nrm$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_nrm$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_agvhd$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_agvhd$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(>1) = %.0f%%", or_cmv$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_cmv$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(>1) = %.0f%%", or_bsi$p_dir * 100), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_ifi$p_dir * 100) ) ) summary_tbl |> kable(align = c("l", "c", "c", "c")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ### Mechanistic Framework The findings resolve into a unified framework built on two separable consequences of PTCy: 1. **GVHD suppression pathway** (intended): PTCy → reduced aGVHD → less steroid exposure → lower NRM → improved OS. The NRM benefit is fully steroid-mediated; the OS benefit is only partially mediated, suggesting an additional direct contribution. 2. **T-cell lymphodepletion pathway** (unintended): PTCy depletes CMV-specific and bacterial-specific T cells during engraftment. The CMV direction reversal across comparisons confirms this is a depth-of-depletion effect rather than a PTCy-specific one. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 8 %%| label: fig-mechanism %%| fig-cap: "Dual-pathway mechanistic framework for PTCy effects." flowchart LR PTCy --> A["↓ Alloreactive\nT cells"] PTCy --> B["↓ Pathogen-specific\nT cells"] A --> C["↓ aGVHD\nOR 0.59–0.67"] C --> D["↓ Steroid\nexposure"] D --> E["↓ NRM\n(fully mediated)"] D --> F["↓ OS\n(partially mediated)"] B --> G["↑ CMV vs CNI\nOR ~1.4"] B --> H["↓ CMV vs ATG\nOR ~0.8"] B --> I["↑ BSI\nOR ~2.0–2.4"] style A fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style B fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style C fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style G fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style H fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style I fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a ``` --- *Navigate to individual pages using the menu above for detailed results, model diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, GRADE assessments, and risk-of-bias evaluation.* ::: {.callout-tip} ## Post-Block-9 Update (2026-05-29) This analysis includes 251 studies (525 arms, 14 RCTs) extracted through Block 9, an expansion from the original 220-study baseline.
